items.mathematical_reasoning_or_economic_logic: Poverty-trap disincentive from benefit withdrawal: gradual taper removes higher marginal withdrawal
Absolute poverty means inability to afford essentials; relative poverty measures income position
Targeted transfers can focus resources on need; identical payments do not equalise incomes
Cap-and-trade total permitted pollution fixed by permit quantity, conditional on monitoring
Private ownership may alter cost-efficiency incentives, but without guaranteed improvement
Default pension enrollment with free opt-out is a behavioural nudge
Monopsony raising wages for all workers implies marginal labour expenditure above wage
MRP of additional worker: four units each $9 MR = $36, not four times selling price
Price inflation lowers domestic value while simultaneous nominal appreciation raises external value
Bad subsidy uptake forecast causes budget crowd-out and government failure
Rising expected inflation shifts SR Phillips curve upward
Demand expansion moves along fixed SR Phillips curve: lower unemployment, higher inflation
